summary: Both mean 'a bit', but they sit in different places and say different things. 有点儿 goes BEFORE an adjective or verb and reports how things are, usually a complaint: 有点儿贵 'a bit (too) expensive'. 一点儿 goes AFTER an adjective to mean 'a bit more' (便宜一点儿 'a bit cheaper') or BEFORE a noun to mean 'a little of' (一点儿水). 儿 is optional in writing (一点, 有点).

subs.label: 有点儿 + adjective / verb
subs.focus: Force 有点儿 before an adjective or feeling verb to state a mild, usually unwelcome present fact (有点儿贵, 有点儿不舒服, 有点儿担心). Errors: 一点儿 in that slot (一点儿贵), 有点儿 after the adjective, adding 很. No comparison or request in the sentence, so 一点儿 is impossible.

subs.label: adjective + 一点儿
subs.focus: Force 一点儿 after the adjective for 'a bit more': comparison (比 or implied) or a request (快一点儿, 便宜一点儿吧, 大一点儿的). Errors: 很 in a 比 sentence, 有点儿 in a request, 一点儿 before the adjective. 比…有点儿热 is colloquial: never judge-wrong. Include 比, 请, 吧, 的 or a clear wish for change so 有点儿 is ruled out.

subs.label: 有点儿 before vs 一点儿 after
subs.focus: Same-adjective head-to-head: complaint about the present state (这双鞋有点儿小) vs the change wanted or a comparison (有没有大一点儿的). Learner decides state vs change, then which side of the adjective. Two-clause and order items are ideal. Error: one fixed word and position for 'a bit'.

subs.label: 一点儿 + noun
subs.focus: Force 一点儿 before a noun for a small amount (喝一点儿水, 会说一点儿汉语, 还有一点儿时间). Errors: 有点儿 between verb and noun (喝有点儿水), 一点儿 after the noun. Use a clear main verb; if it is 有, make it plainly 'to have' (还有一点儿钱).

subs.label: 一点儿也不 / 都不 / 也没
subs.focus: Force 'not at all' = 一点儿 (+ noun) + 也/都 + 不/没 + adjective/verb (一点儿也不贵, 一点儿钱也没有). Errors: 有点儿也不, 不一点儿贵, 不贵一点儿, and mixing 有点儿不 ('a bit un-') with 一点儿也不. English cue must say 'at all'. Never make 也 vs 都 the choice.

subs.label: 一下 vs 一点儿
subs.focus: Choose verb + 一下 (brief action: 等一下, 问一下, 休息一下) vs 一点儿 (degree after adjective, amount before noun). Errors: 等一点儿, 快一下. Use verbs with no amount (等, 问, 休息, 介绍) for 一下 and adjectives for 一点儿; avoid bare 吃___ / 喝___ frames, where both work.

subs.label: 一些 'some'
subs.focus: Force 一些 + noun for 'some' countable things or people (一些朋友, 一些问题), where 一点儿 fails; recognise adjective + 一些 and 有些 + adjective. Errors: 一点儿朋友, 一些贵, 一些也不. Never force a choice between 好一些 and 好一点儿, or between 有些 and 有点儿; both are right.

rules.rule: To say something is 'a bit' or 'a bit too' something right now, put 有点儿 before the adjective. No 很, no 是.

examples.py: jīn tiān yǒu diǎn r lěng
examples.en: It's a bit cold today.

examples.py: zhè jiàn yī fu yǒu diǎn r guì
examples.en: This piece of clothing is a bit expensive.

examples.zh: 我有点儿累，想早点儿睡觉。
examples.py: wǒ yǒu diǎn r lèi xiǎng zǎo diǎn r shuì jiào
examples.en: I'm a bit tired and want to go to bed early.

rules.note: 有点儿 usually carries a complaint, so it sounds odd with things you are pleased about (好吃, 漂亮, 高兴); for those use 挺 or 很. It is fine with neutral words when the result is not what you wanted. 有一点儿 is the full form and means the same.

rules.rule: 有点儿 also goes before feeling verbs and before 不 + a positive word.
rules.pattern: Subject + 有点儿 + Verb of feeling / 不 + Adjective

examples.py: wǒ yǒu diǎn r xiǎng jiā
examples.en: I'm a bit homesick.

examples.py: tā jīn tiān yǒu diǎn r bù gāo xìng
examples.en: He's a bit unhappy today.

examples.zh: 我有点儿担心明天的考试。
examples.py: wǒ yǒu diǎn r dān xīn míng tiān de kǎo shì
examples.en: I'm a bit worried about tomorrow's exam.

rules.rule: In a comparison, 'a bit more' is 一点儿 after the adjective. 很 cannot go in a 比 sentence, and 有点儿 before the adjective is not the standard form there.
rules.pattern: A + 比 + B + Adjective + 一点儿

examples.py: jīn tiān bǐ zuó tiān lěng yī diǎn r
examples.en: Today is a bit colder than yesterday.

examples.py: dì di bǐ wǒ gāo yī diǎn r
examples.en: My younger brother is a bit taller than me.

examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān hǎo yī diǎn r le
examples.en: I'm a bit better today.

rules.note: The comparison can be unspoken: 好一点儿了 means 'a bit better than before'. In casual speech you will hear 比昨天有点儿热; the form to produce is 比昨天热一点儿.

rules.rule: To ask for a change ('a bit faster, a bit cheaper'), put 一点儿 after the adjective. After a verb the order is verb + adjective + 一点儿.
rules.pattern: (Verb) + Adjective + 一点儿 (+ 吧 / 的)

examples.py: qǐng shuō màn yī diǎn r
examples.en: Please speak a bit more slowly.

examples.py: pián yi yī diǎn r ba
examples.en: Make it a bit cheaper, will you?

examples.zh: 你快一点儿，我们要迟到了。
examples.py: nǐ kuài yī diǎn r wǒ men yào chí dào le
examples.en: Hurry up a bit, we're going to be late.

rules.note: In speech 一 is often dropped here: 快点儿, 便宜点儿.

rules.rule: Describing how it is now: 有点儿 before the adjective. Saying how you want it, or comparing: 一点儿 after the adjective. Never the other way round.
rules.pattern: 有点儿 + Adjective (state)  /  Adjective + 一点儿 (change, comparison)

examples.zh: 这双鞋有点儿小，有没有大一点儿的？
examples.py: zhè shuāng xié yǒu diǎn r xiǎo yǒu méi yǒu dà yī diǎn r de
examples.en: These shoes are a bit small; do you have slightly bigger ones?

examples.zh: 这个房间有点儿小，那个大一点儿。
examples.py: zhè ge fáng jiān yǒu diǎn r xiǎo nà ge dà yī diǎn r
examples.en: This room is a bit small; that one is a bit bigger.

examples.zh: 你说得有点儿快，请说慢一点儿。
examples.py: nǐ shuō de yǒu diǎn r kuài qǐng shuō màn yī diǎn r
examples.en: You're speaking a bit fast; please speak a bit more slowly.

rules.rule: 'A little (of something)' is 一点儿 before the noun, after the verb. 有点儿 cannot follow another verb.

examples.py: wǒ xiǎng hē yī diǎn r shuǐ
examples.en: I'd like to drink a little water.

examples.py: tā huì shuō yī diǎn r hàn yǔ
examples.en: He can speak a little Chinese.

examples.py: wǒ zhǐ chī le yī diǎn r mǐ fàn
examples.en: I only ate a little rice.

examples.py: wǒ men hái yǒu yī diǎn r shí jiān
examples.en: We still have a little time.

rules.note: In 还有一点儿时间 the 有 is the verb 'to have' followed by 一点儿 + noun; it is not the adverb 有点儿. After a verb 一 is often dropped in speech: 喝点儿水.

rules.rule: 'Not at all' is 一点儿 + 也 or 都 + 不 + adjective or verb. 也 and 都 are interchangeable here.
rules.pattern: Subject + 一点儿 + 也/都 + 不 + Adjective / Verb

examples.py: zhè ge cài yī diǎn r yě bù là
examples.en: This dish isn't spicy at all.

examples.py: wǒ yī diǎn r dōu bù lèi
examples.en: I'm not tired at all.

examples.zh: 他一点儿也不喜欢运动。
examples.py: tā yī diǎn r yě bù xǐ huan yùn dòng
examples.en: He doesn't like exercise at all.

rules.note: 一 is not dropped in this pattern, and 有点儿 cannot replace 一点儿. Compare 有点儿不舒服 'a bit unwell' with 一点儿也不舒服 'not comfortable at all'.

rules.rule: For something that did not happen or does not exist at all, use 没 instead of 不. A noun goes between 一点儿 and 也/都.
rules.pattern: 一点儿 (+ Noun) + 也/都 + 没(有) + Verb

examples.py: wǒ yī diǎn r yě méi tīng dǒng
examples.en: I didn't understand any of it.

examples.py: tā yī diǎn r dōng xi dōu méi chī
examples.en: He didn't eat anything at all.

examples.py: wǒ yī diǎn r qián yě méi yǒu
examples.en: I have no money at all.

rules.rule: Verb + 一下 means do the action briefly or 'just do it'; it softens a request. It counts the action, not an amount.

examples.py: qǐng děng yī xià
examples.en: Please wait a moment.

examples.py: wǒ men xiū xi yī xià ba
examples.en: Let's take a short break.

examples.py: nǐ wèn yī xià lǎo shī ba
examples.en: Go and ask the teacher.

rules.rule: 一下 follows an action verb; 一点儿 follows an adjective or stands before a noun. So: 等一下, but 快一点儿 and 喝一点儿水.
rules.pattern: Verb + 一下  /  Adjective + 一点儿  /  Verb + 一点儿 + Noun

examples.py: nǐ kàn yī xià zhè běn shū
examples.en: Have a look at this book.

examples.py: nǐ zǒu kuài yī diǎn r
examples.en: Walk a bit faster.

examples.zh: 你先坐一下，喝一点儿茶。
examples.py: nǐ xiān zuò yī xià hē yī diǎn r chá
examples.en: Sit down for a moment first and have a little tea.

rules.note: With eating and drinking verbs both can appear with different meanings: 吃一点儿 'eat a little (of it)', 尝一下 'have a taste'.

rules.rule: 一些 + noun means 'some, a few'. Use it (or 几 + measure word) for people and things you count; 一点儿 is for a small amount of something you do not count.

examples.py: wǒ mǎi le yī xiē shuǐ guǒ
examples.en: I bought some fruit.

examples.zh: 我有一些问题想问老师。
examples.py: wǒ yǒu yī xiē wèn tí xiǎng wèn lǎo shī
examples.en: I have some questions I'd like to ask the teacher.

examples.zh: 他在北京认识了一些中国朋友。
examples.py: tā zài běi jīng rèn shi le yī xiē zhōng guó péng you
examples.en: He got to know some Chinese friends in Beijing.

rules.note: With mass nouns both are possible and 一些 simply suggests more: 喝一点儿水 'a little water', 喝一些水 'some water'.

rules.rule: After an adjective, 一些 works like 一点儿 ('a bit more'). Before an adjective, the partner of 有点儿 is 有些, never 一些. 'Not at all' only takes 一点儿.
rules.pattern: Adjective + 一些  /  有些 + Adjective

examples.py: wǒ jīn tiān jué de hǎo yī xiē le
examples.en: I feel somewhat better today.

examples.py: zhè jiàn bǐ nà jiàn cháng yī xiē
examples.en: This one is a bit longer than that one.

examples.py: tā zuì jìn yǒu xiē bù gāo xìng
examples.en: He's been somewhat unhappy lately.

rules.note: 有些 + adjective sounds a little more formal than 有点儿.

right.py: zhè jiàn yī fu yǒu diǎn r guì
right.en: This piece of clothing is a bit expensive.

contrasts.why: Before an adjective, 'a bit' is 有点儿. 一点儿 never stands directly in front of an adjective (except in 一点儿也不).

right.py: qǐng shuō màn yī diǎn r
right.en: Please speak a bit more slowly.

contrasts.why: A request for change means 'a bit MORE slowly', so 一点儿 goes after the adjective. 有点儿 only describes how things already are.

right.py: tā bǐ wǒ gāo yī diǎn r
right.en: He's a bit taller than me.

contrasts.why: In a 比 sentence the size of the difference goes after the adjective: 高一点儿. 一点儿 does not stand in front of the adjective.

right.py: wǒ xiǎng hē yī diǎn r shuǐ
right.en: I'd like to drink a little water.

contrasts.why: Before a noun, 'a little' is 一点儿. 有点儿 is an adverb and cannot come between a verb and its object.

right.py: wǒ yī diǎn r yě bù lèi

contrasts.why: 'Not at all' is the fixed frame 一点儿 + 也/都 + 不. 有点儿 cannot enter it.

right.py: zhè ge cài yī diǎn r yě bù là
right.en: This dish isn't spicy at all.

contrasts.why: English puts 'at all' at the end; Chinese puts 一点儿也 in front of 不.
Doing an action for a moment is verb + 一下. 一点儿 measures an amount of something or a degree, and waiting has neither.
快 is an adjective; 'a bit more' of a quality is 一点儿. 一下 needs an action verb.

right.py: wǒ yǒu yī xiē zhōng guó péng you

contrasts.why: 一点儿 is a small amount of stuff, not a number of people. For things you count use 一些 or 几个.

right.py: zhè ge cài tǐng hǎo chī de

contrasts.why: 有点儿 sounds like a complaint, so it clashes with praise. For 'quite, pretty' with something good use 挺...的 or 很.

cheat: Complaining about how it is now? 有点儿 BEFORE the adjective: 有点儿贵.
'A bit MORE', a request, or 比 in the sentence? 一点儿 AFTER the adjective: 便宜一点儿.
A noun follows? 一点儿 + noun: 喝一点儿水. Never 有点儿 after another verb.
'At all' in the English? 一点儿 + 也/都 + 不/没, all in front of the adjective or verb.
Action for a moment (等, 看, 问, 休息)? Verb + 一下, not 一点儿.
People or things you count? 一些 or 几个, not 一点儿.
Something good? Not 有点儿; use 挺 or 很.
